target_customer: Private and public companies that want a listing venue and equity management tools aligned with long-term governance, plus long-term institutional investors
problem: Public markets reward quarterly results, which pushes executives toward short-term decisions. LTSE offers an exchange with listing standards that require long-term policies, plus cap table software for companies before they list.
business_model: Exchange revenue from listing fees and trading, plus SaaS subscriptions for LTSE Equity cap table management
product_category: Securities exchange and equity management software

founders.name: Eric Ries
founders.background_notes: Author of The Lean Startup and creator of the Lean Startup method, per the YC page. Education not stated on the sources opened.

founders.name: John Bautista
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page. No background given on the page.

competitors.name: NYSE
competitors.what: Dominant US listing venue for large companies
competitors.traction_then: About 2,800 listed companies with roughly $28 trillion market value per 2016 coverage

competitors.name: Nasdaq
competitors.what: Dominant US listing venue for technology companies
competitors.traction_then: Roughly $10 trillion in listed market value per the same 2016 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching engine and market data are standard exchange engineering, but a new national exchange needs SEC approval, which came in May 2019, and integration with market participants.

defensibility.rationale: An SEC-registered exchange license and its listing rules are hard to copy, but listing venues compete on liquidity and reputation, and LTSE started with zero listings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twilio and Asana dual-listed on LTSE in 2021 alongside their NYSE listings, so incumbents were not displaced. Sources opened show no acquisition.

market_need_then: Eric Ries floated the idea in The Lean Startup epilogue, and 2016 coverage framed a market of founders and investors who wanted alternatives to quarterly reporting pressure. Demand for a distinct exchange was untested.

identity.logo: Blue mark with LTSE text and an X shape with diagonal aqua stripes, per a MEMX case study

branding.brand_signature: The long-term mission framed around Eric Ries and the Lean Startup name
branding.community_and_virality: Substantial press attention at announcement and launch (Bloomberg, Fortune, Quartz). No evidence found of merch or fan communities.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage of the exchange leaned on Eric Ries's reputation and a clear descriptive name, but no source shows the brand itself driving listings or volume.

pivots.to: Exchange plus LTSE Equity cap table software and private market services
pivots.why: The YC description lists LTSE Equity as a product built alongside the exchange. The exact date and reason were not stated in sources opened.

outcome_analysis: LTSE raised about $19M in 2016, a $50M Series B in September 2019 and a reported $100M in June 2022, won SEC approval in May 2019 and began trading in September 2020. It listed Twilio and Asana as dual listings in 2021 and ThredUp in 2023, but its listing business stayed small next to NYSE and Nasdaq. It added LTSE Equity software and petitioned the SEC in 2025 on semiannual reporting. It is active with leadership changes, but its market impact is unproven.
notes: Series A amount and 2016 date come from Wikipedia (about $19M from about 70 investors, date not given there) and a search summary citing Crunchbase of about $18.7M in July 2016. This is a single-source figure, so treat it as approximate. The June 2022 $100M round is from Wikipedia and a Crowdfund Insider report that returned 403 on fetch. Aggregators list about $172M total across six rounds. YC page lists the batch as Summer 2017 with founded 2012. Outcome searches for layoffs returned nothing relevant.
